findings.claim: The hand-written InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions type flattens the zod discriminated union and makes teamId optional for all scopes. A team-scope call without teamId compiles, fails safeParse at runtime and silently returns empty results; this is also inconsistent with InsightsRoutingService's strict union type.

verifier.reason: packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:29-34 adds InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions with teamId?: number across all scopes and uses it in the constructor (line 58), so a team-scope call omitting teamId compiles, fails insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema.safeParse (lines 62-63) to set this.options = null, and returns NOTHING_CONDITION (1=0) at lines 125-128. By contrast, InsightsRoutingService keeps the strict zod-inferred union InsightsRoutingServiceOptions in its constructor at packages/lib/server/service/insightsRouting.ts:29,52.

findings.claim: The org-scope test assertion depends on the order of ids inside ANY(...) arrays. Those ids come from repository queries (findAllByParentId, MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds) without orderBy, so the SQL-fragment equality is nondeterministic.

verifier.reason: In packages/lib/server/service/__tests__/insightsBooking.integration-test.ts:332-343, expect(conditions).toEqual(Prisma.sql`...`) asserts exact array order inside both ANY(...) parameters, which buildOrgAuthorizationCondition (packages/lib/server/service/insightsBooking.ts:150-169) builds without sorting. Neither TeamRepository.findAllByParentId (packages/lib/server/repository/team.ts:192-197) nor MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds (packages/lib/server/repository/membership.ts:409-419) specifies an orderBy clause, making the SQL-fragment equality nondeterministic.
